content.content: A context that cannot be resolved surfaces as a refusal: the resolver's failure is turned into the refusal value the envelope already renders and handed back to the envelope, which writes its single stderr line and returns its status. The entry invents no second surface — the resolution failure leaves by the envelope's channels and status, and the envelope's dispatch never runs.
content.rationale: Resolution runs before the envelope, so a resolution failure has no handler to return through and no verb to blame; the envelope already owns refusal's shape, channel, and status (S4-own, O1, O3) and is the sole writer of both streams (M-output-return), so the entry hands the failure back to the envelope rather than writing a line of its own. The evidence the resolver carried (S3-err) is what the line carries. Only a genuine resolution failure — no jj binary, or a root query that could not run (the two ContextError cases) — reaches this path: a directory with no workspace is not such a failure, resolving to a root-less context (S3-root-optional) instead.
